items.title: [Bug] Hybrid mamba align precopy: illegal memory access on prefix-cache resume with explicit --block-size (state column seeded with wrong block size)
items.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.27.1, V2 GPU runner, single RTX 3090 (SM86), CUDA 12.x, WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 (also reproduces the same way on bare metal by code inspection). Model: Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid GDN/mamba + full attention), W4A16.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`MambaHybridModelState.add_request` (v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py) seeds the running mamba state column with the **CLI/attention block size** instead of the **mamba KV-cache group's block size**:

```python
self._mamba_state_idx_gpu[req_index].fill_(
    (new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size
)
```

On hybrid models the mamba group's `block_size` is derived from page matching (e.g. 2176 for a Qwen3-Next-style hybrid) and generally differs from `cache_config.block_size` whenever the user passes `--block-size` explicitly (required e.g. for quantized-KV setups whose tile size dictates the block, in our case 128).

With `--block-size 128 --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, the **second** request over a cached prefix crashes: a resume with `num_computed_tokens=100096` seeds `state_idx = (100096-1)//128 = 781` instead of `(100096-1)//2176 = 45`. The fused align precopy (`precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel`) then reads `block_table[req, 781]` in a table with only ~61 columns, gets a garbage block id, and dies with:

```
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py", line 201, in preprocess_state
  File "vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py", line 826, in run_fused_precopy
```

(confirmed as the faulting kernel with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`).

First requests are unaffected (`num_computed == 0` seeds `-1` regardless of divisor), so in practice this looks like a spurious crash that only appears on the second request over a >1-block cached prefix — easy to misattribute.

**Repro:** any hybrid (mamba+attention) model with `--block-size <n>` where n != the mamba group block size, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--mamba-cache-mode align`; send the same multi-block prompt twice.

### Fix (verified)

Seed with the mamba spec's block size. `_mamba_spec` is populated lazily by the first batch's `preprocess_state`; a resume can only happen after some batch has run, and fresh requests seed `-1` either way, so the fallback is safe:

```python
mamba_bs = (self._mamba_spec.block_size
            if self._mamba_spec is not None
            else self.cache_config.block_size)
self._mamba_state_idx_gpu[req_index].fill_(
    (new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // mamba_bs
)
```

Verified on the setup above: two-turn 102k-token needle test, turn 2 resumes from 100,096 cached tokens, both answers correct, turn-2 latency 6.3 s vs ~190 s cold. Happy to turn this into a PR if wanted.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: int4 per-token-head KV cache: triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_per_token_head_quant returns wrong values
items.body:
Observed on main @ eac636a7fa476983cdae34b45a984e9852aad375 (NVIDIA H200, driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0).

`tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py::test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head` fails in the int4 branch (`kv_quant_mode=INT4_PER_TOKEN_HEAD`, `quant_min=-8.0`, `quant_max=7.0`): the dequantized round-trip (unpack nibbles → zero-point → scale → inverse RHT) lands far outside the assertion tolerance (atol=rtol=0.5) vs the bf16 reference.

**Deterministic failure** — head_size=64, num_kv_heads=1, num_tokens=42 (seed 0, block_size 16), i.e. `[int4-0-16-64-1-42]`. Fails on every run with identical mismatch statistics (inputs are seed-deterministic):

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
Mismatched elements: 35 / 64 (54.7%)
Greatest absolute difference: 3.0546875 at index (0, 38) (up to 0.5 allowed)
Greatest relative difference: 3651.2666015625 at index (0, 52) (up to 0.5 allowed)
```

**Flaky failures** — pass/fail flips across runs on identical code:

- head_size=128, num_kv_heads=1, num_tokens=42 (`[int4-0-16-128-1-42]`): 64/128 (50.0%) mismatched, abs 4.002 @ (0, 70), rel 25.5 @ (0, 101)
- head_size=64, num_kv_heads=4, num_tokens=7 (`[int4-0-16-64-4-7]`): 149/256 (58.2%) mismatched, abs 3.93 @ (2, 26), rel 256 @ (0, 37)

All int8 and fp8 parametrizations, and the remaining int4 combos, pass consistently.

**Minimal repro:**

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py \
  -k "test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head and int4-0-16-64-1-42"
```

**Analysis:** the kernel under test is `vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_per_token_head_quant` (assertion at `tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py:256`). A deterministic 54.7% element mismatch at ~6x the allowed absolute tolerance rules out tolerance noise and points to a correctness defect in the int4 pack/RHT path (candidate causes: zero-point packing or nibble ordering). The two shape-dependent flaky combos additionally suggest a race or uninitialized/leftover cache state whose manifestation depends on shape/head layout.

The qcfg fixture carries IDs int4/int8/fp8; the stacked parametrize resolves bottom-up, so `[int4-0-16-64-1-42]` = seed 0, block_size 16, head_size 64, num_kv_heads 1, num_tokens 42. All failing combos share seed 0 / block_size 16, but those are the only values in `SEEDS`/`BLOCK_SIZES`, so there is no signal there.

Happy to collect a failing-tensor dump if that helps isolate it.

items.title: [Bug]: MooncakeStoreConnector stores invalid recurrent states with mamba_cache_mode=align, causing silent output corruption
items.body:
### Your current environment

The issue was reproduced on vLLM `main` at:

```text
commit: 0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5
runtime vLLM version: 0.27.2rc1.dev142+g0ad04cff1
Python: 3.12.3
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu129
CUDA runtime: 12.9
GPU: 8 x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (the reproduction uses TP=2)
NVIDIA driver: 580.173.02
mooncake-transfer-engine: 0.3.12.post1
transformers: 5.15.0
triton: 3.7.1
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS
GCC: 13.3.0
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Summary

`MooncakeStoreConnector` can publish external prefix-cache keys for recurrent-state boundaries that do not contain a valid state.

With `MambaSpec(mamba_cache_mode="align")`, vLLM may intentionally leave some logical state boundaries without a materialized recurrent-state block. Such entries use `NULL_BLOCK_ID = 0`. The normal Mooncake Store save path currently resolves that block ID to an address and publishes the corresponding Store key without rejecting the null block.

As a result:

1. A producer publishes a key for a boundary such as token 2112 or 2960 even though no valid GDN/Mamba/ShortConv state was captured there.
2. Mooncake Store lookup sees that the key exists and reports the longer prefix as externally reusable.
3. The consumer loads the bytes successfully and skips recomputation up to that boundary.
4. Generation silently diverges from a cold baseline. There is no Put/Get error, and in some cases the generated tokens remain the same while logprobs differ significantly.

Byte-level instrumentation shows that Mooncake transfers the selected bytes exactly. The invalid all-zero bytes already exist on the producer side because the selected recurrent-state block is `NULL_BLOCK_ID`. This points to invalid key publication in the producer save path, rather than data corruption in Mooncake transport.

### Why this is user-visible

This can affect normal serving whenever all of the following are true:

- a model has recurrent state, for example GDN, Mamba1, Mamba2, or ShortConv;
- `MooncakeStoreConnector` external prefix caching is enabled;
- a long producer request creates Store keys for an intermediate boundary that did not receive a valid recurrent-state snapshot under the producer's prefill/chunking history;
- a later request reuses that boundary.

The request succeeds with HTTP 200 and Mooncake reports successful Put/Get operations, but the model output can be wrong.

### Generic reproduction for recurrent-state models

The same producer/consumer pattern was validated with GDN, Mamba1, Mamba2, and ShortConv caches, on both hybrid and pure recurrent-state models.

The smallest tested profile is `state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf`. The model-specific values used in the successful reproductions are:

| Profile | `MODEL` | State type | Producer repeats | Consumer repeats | Common prefix | Invalid Store hit |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Smallest | `state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf` | pure Mamba1 | 1000 | 1000 | 3026 | 3024 |
| Pure Mamba2 | `mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1` | pure Mamba2 | 1000 | 1000 | 3031 | 3024 |
| ShortConv hybrid | `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-350M` | ShortConv + Full Attention | 1000 | 1000 | 3027 | 3024 |
| Mamba2 hybrid | `Zyphra/Zamba2-1.2B-instruct` | Mamba2 + Full Attention | 1000 | 1000 | 3030 | 2960 |
| GDN hybrid | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` | GDN + Full Attention | 1250 | 700 | 2126 | 2112 |

<details>

<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

All tested runs used TP=2. The commands below are parameterized so any row can be selected. For example, the smallest profile is:

For `mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1`, also pass `--load-format safetensors`. Other model-specific loading flags can be added without changing the producer/consumer sequence.

```bash
export MODEL=state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf
export SERVED_MODEL=mamba-130m-hf
export VERIFICATION_CODE=PURE-MAMBA-STORE
export PRODUCER_REPEATS=1000
export CONSUMER_REPEATS=1000
export PYTHONHASHSEED=0
```

#### 1. Start Mooncake Store

```bash
mooncake_master \
  --port 50061 \
  --default_kv_lease_ttl 30m
```

Save the following configuration as `/tmp/mooncake-store.json`:

```json
{
  "mode": "embedded",
  "metadata_server": "P2PHANDSHAKE",
  "master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50061",
  "global_segment_size": "4GB",
  "local_buffer_size": "1GB",
  "protocol": "tcp",
  "device_name": "",
  "enable_offload": false
}
```

```bash
export MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/mooncake-store.json
```

#### 2. Generate a shared-prefix producer/consumer request pair

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import os

from transformers import AutoTokenizer

model = os.environ["MODEL"]
served_model = os.environ["SERVED_MODEL"]
code = os.environ["VERIFICATION_CODE"]
producer_repeats = int(os.environ["PRODUCER_REPEATS"])
consumer_repeats = int(os.environ["CONSUMER_REPEATS"])

shared = (
    "Cache correctness record. The exact verification code is "
    f"{code}. Remember it for a later question. "
)
producer_prompt = (
    shared
    + "neutral cache context " * producer_repeats
    + "Producer-only task: write the cache and answer ACK:"
)
consumer_prompt = (
    shared
    + "neutral cache context " * consumer_repeats
    + "Consumer-only question: What is the exact verification code? "
      "Answer only with the code:"
)
common = {
    "model": served_model,
    "max_tokens": 16,
    "temperature": 0,
    "seed": 0,
    "logprobs": 1,
}
for path, prompt in (
    ("/tmp/producer-request.json", producer_prompt),
    ("/tmp/consumer-request.json", consumer_prompt),
):
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as output:
        json.dump({**common, "prompt": prompt}, output)

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model, trust_remote_code=True)
producer_ids = tokenizer.encode(producer_prompt, add_special_tokens=True)
consumer_ids = tokenizer.encode(consumer_prompt, add_special_tokens=True)
common_prefix = 0
for producer_id, consumer_id in zip(producer_ids, consumer_ids):
    if producer_id != consumer_id:
        break
    common_prefix += 1
print({
    "producer_tokens": len(producer_ids),
    "consumer_tokens": len(consumer_ids),
    "common_prefix_tokens": common_prefix,
})
PY
```

The important shape is that the common prefix reaches an intermediate Store boundary for which the producer did not retain a recurrent-state snapshot. The exact boundary depends on the model's state-cache page size and tokenizer, so assert the actual external hit metric rather than relying only on prompt character counts.

#### 3. Record a cold baseline

Start vLLM without a KV connector:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name "$SERVED_MODEL" \
  --port 8002 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --mamba-cache-mode align
```

```bash
curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @/tmp/consumer-request.json \
  http://127.0.0.1:8002/v1/completions > /tmp/cold-response.json
```

Stop the baseline server so that the Store consumer can use the same GPUs.

#### 4. Populate Mooncake Store from a producer

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name "$SERVED_MODEL" \
  --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector",
    "kv_role":"kv_producer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{
      "cache_prefix":"state-boundary-repro",
      "enable_lookup":false
    }
  }'
```

```bash
curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @/tmp/producer-request.json \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions > /tmp/producer-response.json
```

Wait until the Put succeeds and becomes visible to Store lookup.

#### 5. Restore the prefix in a separate consumer

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name "$SERVED_MODEL" \
  --port 8002 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector",
    "kv_role":"kv_consumer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{
      "cache_prefix":"state-boundary-repro",
      "enable_lookup":true,
      "load_async":true
    }
  }'
```

```bash
curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @/tmp/consumer-request.json \
  http://127.0.0.1:8002/v1/completions > /tmp/store-response.json
```

</details>

Verify all three conditions:

1. Store metrics show a non-zero external prefix hit and successful Get operations.
2. The Store response differs from the cold response in generated token strings and/or per-token logprobs.
3. Repeating the experiment with `--max-num-batched-tokens` set to the invalid Store-hit boundary makes that boundary a real state-capture boundary; the restored output then exactly matches the cold output. This third step is a diagnostic control, not a general workaround.

### Observed result (Qwen3.5-9B example)

Mooncake Store reports successful operations:

```text
producer: Put 56 keys, 484442112 bytes, 0 failed keys
consumer: Get 14 keys, 121110528 bytes, 0 failed keys
consumer external prefix cache hit: 2112 tokens
```

However, deterministic output differs from the cold baseline:

```text
cold baseline:
 HYBRID-528-GDN.

The exact verification code is

Mooncake Store consumer:
 HYBRID-528-GDN

The exact verification code is HY

maximum absolute per-token logprob difference: 1.4653081893920898
```

The mismatch is deterministic in repeated runs.

### Expected result

An external prefix-cache key should only be published when every state required to resume from that boundary is valid and recoverable.

If the recurrent-state block at a candidate boundary is `NULL_BLOCK_ID`, the producer should not publish that boundary as reusable. Lookup should return the longest earlier boundary that is valid for all required cache groups, and the consumer should recompute the remaining tokens.

For deterministic greedy decoding, a cold run and a correctly restored Store run should produce the same text, generated tokens, and per-token logprobs.

### Root-cause evidence

Instrumentation immediately before Mooncake Put and immediately after Mooncake Get at the 2112-token boundary shows:

```text
Qwen3.5 GDN recurrent states:
  producer states using physical block 0: 6 / 6
  producer states containing only zero bytes: 6 / 6
  producer -> consumer byte-exact matches: 6 / 6
  SHA-256 for every zero state:
    6334891ad0b99640af1d1dd5dc8863447ff79bb5b3d9936f8bcfc98a5c41922d

Qwen3.5 Full Attention KV entries:
  producer entries containing non-zero bytes: 2 / 2
  producer -> consumer byte-exact matches: 2 / 2
```

Therefore:

- the recurrent-state entries are already invalid before transport;
- the Full Attention KV entries are valid;
- Mooncake transfers all selected entries byte-for-byte;
- the failure is caused by publishing a key whose recurrent state resolves to the null block.

As a diagnostic control, adding `--max-num-batched-tokens 2112` to all three servers changes the producer's state-capture boundary:

```text
GDN recurrent states at 2112:
  physical blocks: non-null blocks 1, 2, and 3
  non-zero states: 6 / 6
  producer -> consumer byte-exact matches: 6 / 6

Full Attention KV:
  producer -> consumer byte-exact matches: 2 / 2

output comparison:
  text: exact match
  generated tokens: exact match
  maximum absolute per-token logprob difference: 0.0
```

This is a diagnostic control, not a general production workaround: arbitrary request lengths can expose other intermediate boundaries.

### Cross-model evidence

The same default-vs-aligned experiment was repeated on five full models covering four recurrent-state implementations. `bad boundary` is a boundary advertised by Store lookup under the default scheduler configuration. `null state` is measured on the producer before Put.

| Model | Cache architecture | Page size | Bad boundary | Producer recurrent-state evidence | Mooncake transfer | User-visible result | Aligned control |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | GDN + Full Attention | 528 | 2112 | 6/6 GDN states use null block and are all zero | 8/8 total entries byte-exact | Tokens differ; max logprob diff 1.465308 | Exact at 2112 |
| Zyphra/Zamba2-1.2B-instruct | Mamba2 + Full Attention | 80 | 2960 | 14/14 Mamba2 states use null block and are all zero | 16/16 total entries byte-exact | Tokens differ; max logprob diff 2.302462 | Exact at 2960 |
| LiquidAI/LFM2.5-350M | ShortConv + Full Attention | 16 | 3024 | 4/4 ShortConv states use null block and are all zero | 6/6 total entries byte-exact | Tokens happen to match; max logprob diff 0.150565 | Exact at 3024 |
| state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf | Pure Mamba1 | 16 | 3024 | 2/2 Mamba1 states use null block and are all zero | 2/2 entries byte-exact | Tokens differ; max logprob diff 2.436541 | Exact at 3024 |
| mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1 | Pure Mamba2 | 16 | 3024 | 2/2 Mamba2 states use null block and are all zero | 2/2 entries byte-exact | Tokens differ; max logprob diff 2.756008 | Exact at 3024 |

The pure Mamba results show that hybrid Full Attention groups are not required to trigger the bug.

### Suspected code path

All links below point to the tested commit.

1. [`NULL_BLOCK_ID` is defined as block 0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py#L46).
2. [`MambaManager.remove_skipped_blocks()` replaces skipped state blocks with the null block](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L1431-L1459).
3. [`ChunkedTokenDatabase.prepare_values()` resolves logical chunks through `block_ids` and computes transfer addresses](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/data.py#L211-L241), but does not reject `NULL_BLOCK_ID`.
4. The normal save path [builds keys from processed token ranges](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py#L838-L848), [prepares the addresses](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py#L918-L928), and [submits the batch Put](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py#L967-L975) without filtering null state blocks.
5. In contrast, the [partial-tail save path already skips `NULL_BLOCK_ID`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py#L675-L686).

The ordinary save path appears to need equivalent validity handling while keeping token ranges, keys, group indices, addresses, and sizes aligned.

### Suggested fix direction

One possible minimal fix is to reject a candidate Store boundary when any recurrent-state group resolves to NULL_BLOCK_ID. More generally, the save path should only publish a boundary after verifying that all cache groups required to resume from that boundary are recoverable.

### Related issues and PRs

I searched existing vLLM issues and PRs for `MooncakeStoreConnector`, `NULL_BLOCK_ID`, recurrent/Mamba state boundaries, skipped blocks, and incorrect-output reports. I did not find an issue or PR that already contains this exact, directly reproduced normal-save-path failure.

The closest existing report is #50630:

- #50630 describes a broader missing-capability/boundary-invariant problem around recurrent caches. It explicitly lists write-side chunk fragmentation, where a recurrent snapshot is registered under a block hash for a different boundary, as an open class.
- However, #50630 focuses primarily on EAGLE/MTP cache-peek behavior and states that it had not established whether the write-side path was reachable on `main`.
- This report directly demonstrates reachability without EAGLE, MTP, speculative decoding, or P/D disaggregation. It isolates the ordinary `MooncakeStoreConnector` Put path, identifies `NULL_BLOCK_ID` before Put, proves byte-exact Put/Get, and reproduces silent output divergence on five models.

<details>

<summary>Other related but distinct work</summary>

| Issue / PR | Relationship | Difference from this report |
|---|---|---|
| #49499 | Mooncake Store silent recurrent-state corruption with TP > 1 | Fixed TP-shard dedup/keying. The tested commit already contains this fix; here each transferred entry matches its producer bytes, but the producer bytes come from the null block. |
| #49502 | Mooncake Store partial-tail and read-side hit-boundary handling | Addresses reliable partial-tail offload and lookup-side boundaries. This report exercises ordinary full-entry save and invalid key publication on the write side. |
| #44451 / #44488 | Skipped/null Mamba blocks make KV-event token/hash mapping ambiguous | Concerns `BlockStored` event metadata. This report concerns actual Mooncake Store keys and state payloads used for inference. |
| #43559 / #51113 / #51351 | Recurrent-cache poisoning and capability handling with EAGLE/MTP | #51113 fixes mid-block state published as an aligned state under EAGLE/MTP. The tested commit contains it; this reproduction enables neither EAGLE nor MTP and instead finds a null source block in the ordinary Store save path. |
| #51468 | External Mamba-state/local Full Attention hit divergence | Fixes an assertion in partial-tail truncation after local eviction. This report uses ordinary prefix matching and reaches successful inference with silently incorrect state. |
| #49757 | Stale block-table rows during dummy runs | Prevents dummy kernels from overwriting externally loaded recurrent state. This report captures invalid bytes before Put, rather than consumer state overwritten after Get. |
| #49360 | `MooncakeStoreConnector` hang on a GDN model | A transport/liveness failure under EFA and offload pressure, rather than successful retrieval followed by silent incorrect output. |

</details>


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug][Spec Decode] All-NaN logits row is laundered into an out-of-vocab token id by the rejection sampler (device assert far from origin); NaN-metric blind spot on the verify path; uninit-scratch audit
items.body:
## TL;DR

If any verification row of `target_logits` is all-NaN (numerics upset in the model forward — whatever the cause), the V2 GPU-worker rejection sampler does not fail or fall back: its NaN-poisoned block-argmax chain **emits a token id equal to `vocab_size` exactly**, which propagates through `last_sampled_tokens` → `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens` → `input_ids` and detonates 1–3 steps later as:

```
/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Indexing.cu:1524: indexSelectSmallIndex:
Assertion `srcIndex < srcSelectDimSize` failed.
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

surfacing asynchronously (typically in `AsyncOutput.get_output → copy_event.synchronize()`), far from the origin. We reproduced and instrumented this end-to-end ~10 times. Open issue #42261 (gemma4 + MTP, same assert, intermittent, restart clears it) matches this signature and is plausibly the same bug.

Independently, the engine's only NaN detector cannot see these rows (§ NaN-metric gap), and the same file contains a family of latent uninitialized-scratch hazards (§ audit).

## Mechanism (fully instrumented)

Configuration: spec decode (dspark; greedy drafts → one-hot verification path), FULL decode cudagraphs, TP4, sustained mixed traffic. All findings verified against `main` as of 2026-08-17.

1. A verification row of `target_logits` arrives **all-NaN** (in our case the numerics fault was in a custom SM80 attention kernel amplifying garbage KV reads — not upstream's code — but any NaN row triggers the rest).
2. In the verify kernel, acceptance comparisons against NaN are false → the position is rejected.
3. `_rejection_resample_kernel` computes the one-hot residual of the NaN row (still NaN), adds gumbel noise (still NaN), and stores per-block maxima/argmaxes. Captured block dump from a live event, `RESAMPLE_BLOCK_SIZE=1024`, vocab 129280 → 127 blocks:
   ```
   local_max[0..125] = NaN            (argmax = each block's last lane — NaN-poisoned tl.max)
   local_max[126]    = -inf           (its 768 masked padding lanes beat NaN in this comparator order)
   local_argmax[126] = 129280         (= 126*1024 + 256, the first PADDED lane)
   ```
4. `_insert_resampled_kernel`'s cross-block `tl.argmax` over `[NaN ×126, -inf]` is NaN-poisoned and selects block 126, loads `local_argmax[126] = 129280 = vocab_size`, and **stores it into a valid slot of `sampled`**.
5. `post_update` copies it to `last_sampled_tokens`; the next step's `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens` writes it into `input_ids`; the embedding gather asserts.

The failure is worse than the crash: a NaN row whose position is *not* resampled samples an arbitrary in-vocab token **silently**. The crash is the detectable minority.

## Evidence highlights

- Bounds guard on the padded `input_ids` window captured the poison pre-crash across multiple events: always exactly `vocab_size` (129280), always via the resample-insert store (per-store clamp counters), `is_bonus` both true and false across events.
- Winning-block value bit pattern captured in-kernel: `0xFF800000` (-inf) at block 126 with NaN elsewhere (full 127-block dump above).
- With clamp-at-store instrumentation the engine survives indefinitely (45+ contained events in one window), confirming the single injection point.
- Race hypotheses excluded by measurement: a cross-kernel greedy-bit disagreement counter read **zero** across >8k steps while mints continued.

## NaN-metric gap

`VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` / `corrupted_requests_total` is implemented in `Sampler.sample()` — which the spec-decode verification path never calls. During all of the above, the metric read 0. The engine is blind to NaN logits exactly where they get converted into OOB tokens. Suggest computing `num_nans` on the verification logits as well.

## Proposed fixes

1. **Guard degenerate rows in the resample chain** (minimal): after the cross-block argmax, validate the selected token id (`0 <= id < vocab_size`) and the winning value (finite); on failure, fall back deterministically (e.g., token 0 or the request's last valid token) and increment a corruption counter. This converts undefined behavior into a counted, bounded event.
2. **Close the NaN-metric gap** so operators can see degenerate rows on the spec path.
3. Optionally: make `tl.max`/`tl.argmax` consumers in this file NaN-safe by masking non-finite values to `-inf` before reduction (several sites).

## Audit: latent uninitialized-scratch hazards in the same file

While isolating the above we audited `rejection_sampler_utils.py` and found a systemic pattern: **per-request temperature is re-loaded independently by each kernel of a step** (4 independent loads), and those reads gate *writes* to `new_empty` scratch buffers that later kernels *read* under their own temperature load. Nothing enforces agreement (the sampling-state buffers are persistent device arrays updated between steps; async scheduling lets updates land between kernel launches). Five instances:

| # | Producer that skips the write | Buffer | Consumer | Worst case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | stats kernel non-greedy branch skips argmax store | `target_local_argmax` | verify kernel greedy path | uninit int64 emitted as a token id |
| 2 | resample kernel greedy-non-bonus early return | `resampled_local_{argmax,max}` | insert kernel | uninit int64 emitted as a token id |
| 3 | stats kernel greedy branch skips sumexp | `target_local_sumexp` (+draft) | verify non-greedy accept path | garbage acceptance probabilities |
| 4 | `_compute_cumulative_log_p_kernel` `if temp==0: return` | `cumulative_log_p` | 3 gated read sites | `exp(uninit)` ratios (block-verification mode) |
| 5 | residual-mass kernel early returns | `local_residual_mass` | `_compute_global_residual_mass` | garbage residuals (block-verification mode) |

We hit none of these in production traffic (measured disagreements = 0), but they are trivially fixable (write unconditionally — the values are already computed or nearly free) and the class-level fix (snapshot sampling params once per step for all kernels) closes present and future instances at once. Zero-initializing the scratch is cheap hardening.

## Environment

- Observed on vLLM 0.27.1; all cited code verified present on `main` (2026-08-17).
- 8×A100 (SM80), TP4, `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, prefix caching, fp8 KV.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash + dspark (greedy drafts). The NaN *source* in our reproduction was a custom SM80 kernel (not upstream code); the laundering, metric gap, and audit findings are upstream and model-agnostic — any NaN row from any cause takes the same path.

## Reproduction sketch

Inject a single all-NaN row into `target_logits` for one verification position (or run any setup that can produce one) under spec decode with rejection sampling; within that step, `sampled` receives a token id ≥ `vocab_size` (frequently exactly `vocab_size`), and the engine dies on the embedding gather 1–3 steps later with the assert cascade above.

items.title: [Bug]: `find_mm_placeholders` may return an incorrect position for `PromptInsertion`
items.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

When `PromptInsertion` inserts tokens that overlap with adjacent tokens in the original prompt, `find_mm_placeholders` may locate an earlier occurrence instead of the tokens inserted by the prompt update.

For example:

- Original prompt contains `[32000]` at index 3.
- The insertion target is `[32000]`.
- The inserted placeholder tokens are `[32000, 32000]`.

After applying the update, the resulting sequence around the target is:

```text
[..., 32000, 32000, 32000, ...]
      original  inserted
```

The inserted placeholder starts at index 4. However, `find_mm_placeholders` scans the resulting prompt for `[32000, 32000]` and finds the sequence starting at index 3, which includes one token from the original prompt.

## Expected behavior

The placeholder position should refer to the tokens inserted by `PromptInsertion`, so `start_idx` should be 4.

## Actual behavior

`find_mm_placeholders` reports `start_idx=3`.

items.title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 silent output corruption in 1P1D NIXL Direct-PD disaggregated deployment
items.body: ### Summary I am seeing intermittent silent output corruption / garbled generation when serving Kimi-K3 with TP=8 in a 1P1D disaggregated Prefill/Decode deployment using MooncakeStoreConnector together with NixlConnector through MultiConnector. The important A/B observation is: - **NIXL-only PD**: stable, no garbled output observed. - **NIXL + MooncakeStoreConnector through MultiConnector**: garbled output reproducibly appears under sustained load. - **Mooncake enabled + DSpark/speculative decoding disabled**: corruption still reproduces. - **Mooncake disabled**: corruption has not reproduced in my testing. Therefore speculative decoding does not appear to be required to trigger the corruption. The corrupted requests can generate long sequences of nonsensical mixed-language/repeated tokens, for example repeated words such as `Effective/effective` mixed with unrelated English/Chinese fragments. Some affected streams eventually surface at the application layer as HTTP 502 / `7104_UPSTREAM_STREAM_INTERRUPTED`. This looks like a correctness issue rather than a crash-only issue: the engine can continue running while individual outputs are already corrupted. ### Deployment topology Two-node 1P1D deployment: ``` Prefill node Kimi-K3 TP=8 | | NIXL PD transfer v Decode node Kimi-K3 TP=8 ``` Failing configuration additionally uses: ``` Prefill | +-- MultiConnector | +-- NixlConnector | kv_role=kv_producer | +-- MooncakeStoreConnector kv_role=kv_both load_async=true lookup_async=true ``` The Decode node remains a NixlConnector consumer. ### Environment - **Model**: Kimi-K3 - **Tensor parallel size**: 8 - **PD topology**: 1 Prefill + 1 Decode - **KV transfer**: NIXL - **Prefix caching**: enabled - **KV cache dtype**: fp8 - **MLA prefill backend**: FLASHINFER - **VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT**: DS - **vLLM version**: Latest main / nightly - **vLLM commit**: Latest main - **GPU**: 8x NVIDIA B300 - **CUDA**: CUDA 12.8 - **OS / container image**: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 / Container) Relevant upstream fixes included: - #48425: yes (tested on latest main) - #49499: yes (tested on latest main) - #49502: yes (tested on latest main) - #50344: yes (tested on latest main) ### Failing Prefill configuration Relevant environment: ```bash export VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS export VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=4608 ``` KV connector: ```json KV='{ "kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "connectors": [ { "kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail" }, { "kv_connector": "MooncakeStoreConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "load_async": true, "lookup_async": true } } ] } }' ``` Relevant server arguments: ```bash vllm serve /modules/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config \ '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --enforce-eager \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --kv-transfer-config "$KV" ``` *(For minimal reproduction, run without `--speculative-config`, as the corruption reproduces without DSpark).* ### Decode configuration The Decode side uses NIXL only: ```bash vllm serve /modules/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config \ '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --kv-transfer-config \ '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' \ --compilation-config \ '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 ``` ### Stable control configuration If I remove `MooncakeStoreConnector` / `MultiConnector` and use only: ```json --kv-transfer-config \ '{ "kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail" }' ``` on the Prefill side, the same Kimi-K3 TP8 PD setup is stable in my testing. The control setup still uses: - Kimi-K3 - TP=8 - prefix caching enabled - FP8 KV cache - FLASHINFER MLA prefill - NIXL PD transfer I have also tested DSpark/speculative decoding in the NIXL-only configuration without observing the same corruption. ### Reproduction A minimal A/B reproduction: 1. **Test A — Control**: - Start Kimi-K3 TP8 Prefill with NixlConnector only. - Start Kimi-K3 TP8 Decode with NixlConnector. - Enable prefix caching. - Run sustained concurrent traffic, including repeated/shared prefixes. - Confirm prefix-cache activity. - **Result**: No corrupted output observed. 2. **Test B — Failing**: - Keep the same model and PD topology, but replace the Prefill connector with `MultiConnector` (`NixlConnector` + `MooncakeStoreConnector`). - Run the same traffic and make sure Mooncake external cache hits are occurring. - **Result**: Intermittent silent output corruption / garbled text. 3. **Test C — DSpark disabled**: - Repeat Test B without any `--speculative-config`. - **Result**: Corruption still reproduces. (Speculative decoding is not the primary trigger). ### Actual behavior Affected generations suddenly degrade into nonsensical output containing repeated and unrelated multilingual tokens. Example pattern: ``` ... effective ... Effective ... effective ... ... random unrelated English words ... ... Chinese fragments ... ... repeated/degenerate text ... ``` The server does not necessarily crash immediately. At the upper service layer, affected streams can end as: ``` HTTP 502 7104_UPSTREAM_STREAM_INTERRUPTED ``` ### Attachments I can provide: - screenshot of a corrupted generation; - Prometheus graphs from the failing run; - Prometheus graphs from the stable/control run; - complete Prefill/Decode logs around an affected request; - Mooncake hit/load metrics; - exact request ID / prompt and response if needed. ### Additional observation about speculative decoding When DSpark is enabled, I have also observed abnormal MTP/spec-decode acceptance behavior during some bad runs. However, I currently consider this a secondary symptom, because the output corruption can still reproduce after DSpark is completely disabled. Therefore this report is specifically about the Mooncake/external hybrid-cache path, rather than the DSpark rejection sampler. ### Expected behavior Loading a prefix from MooncakeStore should be correctness-equivalent to either: 1. recomputing the prefix, or 2. serving the same prefix from local GPU prefix cache. For Kimi-K3, all cache/state groups required to resume generation should represent the same safe token boundary. Enabling Mooncake external caching should not change model output correctness. ### Suspected area The A/B result suggests the issue is somewhere in the interaction between: - Kimi-K3 hybrid cache - `MooncakeStoreConnector` + `MultiConnector` - external prefix cache lookup/load - KDA recurrent state / attention KV reconciliation A possible failure mode would be a resume boundary where the attention KV and KDA recurrent state do not correspond to the same token position. I am particularly interested in whether the following invariant is always guaranteed for Mooncake external hits: ``` reported reusable prefix <= safe Full-Attention/MLA prefix <= valid boundary with corresponding KDA recurrent state ``` and whether all hybrid cache groups are invalidated/reconciled together if one external group is unavailable or has a shorter valid hit. ### Possibly related issues / PRs - #48425 — per-group prefix-hit divergence for hybrid models with KV connector - #49499 — Mooncake TP-sharded Mamba/linear-attention state corruption - #49502 — reliable partial-tail KV offload for sub-block prompts - #50344 — divergent hybrid cache hits scoped to capable connectors / MultiConnector behavior - #47812 — group-aware recovery for KV load failures on hybrid models - #50630 — hybrid recurrent-cache correctness / hit-boundary coordination discussion If my commit already contains them, this may indicate a remaining Kimi-K3-specific or MooncakeStore/MultiConnector-specific correctness path.

items.title: [Bug]: Triton MoE and block-FP8 GEMMs mishandle the K tile — an out-of-bounds weight read, and wrong scales when a tile spans two quantization groups
items.body:
## Summary

Two Triton GEMMs used by quantized MoE serving get the K tile wrong, and in both cases a sibling code path already does it correctly.

1. **`fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` reads the packed weights out of bounds.** The kernel builds `k_mask` whenever `K` is not a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K` and applies it to the scale load and to *both* zero-point loads, but the weight load itself is unmasked, so the last K iteration reads past the end of the weight tensor. The sibling `fused_moe_kernel` masks the identical load. The numbers that come back are multiplied by a scale that *is* masked to zero, so the arithmetic result is unaffected — this is a memory-safety bug, not a numerical one.

2. **`w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` can pick one scale for a tile that spans several quantization groups.** `_w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` reads a single scale pair per K tile, indexed by `(k * BLOCK_SIZE_K) // group_k`, which is correct only when `BLOCK_SIZE_K` divides `group_k`. Nothing enforces it, and the comment above the default config states the requirement inverted — "BLOCK_SIZE_K must be divisible by block_size[1]" — which is exactly the configuration that breaks. The fused-MoE launcher clamps this (`BLOCK_SIZE_K = min(BLOCK_SIZE_K, min(block_shape[0], block_shape[1]))`); this one does not.

Neither is caught today because the shipped defaults stay inside the safe range: `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm`'s default config sets `BLOCK_SIZE_K = block_k`, and `test_fused_moe_wn16` only uses `k` values of 128 and 1024, which are multiples of every `BLOCK_SIZE_K` the untuned path picks. The exposure in both cases is the tuning-config lookup, which reads `BLOCK_SIZE_K` straight out of a JSON file in `configs/` — and the wna16 files there already carry `BLOCK_SIZE_K` values of 128 (168 entries) and 256 (118 entries).

The GPTQ/AWQ MoE kernel was added in #12185 and the block-FP8 GEMM in #11523.

## Reproduction

Both scripts drive the library's own launchers — `dispatch_fused_moe_kernel` and `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` compute the grid and every kernel argument — against this repo at HEAD, installed with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 pip install -e .`.

**1. Out-of-bounds weight read.** An int4 `w4a16` MoE matmul through `invoke_fused_moe_kernel`, with `K = 96` and `BLOCK_SIZE_K = 64`. The packed weight tensor is `[E, N, K // 2]` uint8, so each row holds 48 bytes while the loop covers 64. The weight tensor is allocated last so that the overrun lands in unallocated memory rather than in a neighbouring tensor, which is what makes it visible to `compute-sanitizer`.

```
$ PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck python repro_gptq_awq.py

  K= 128 BLOCK_SIZE_K= 64: qweight holds 64 bytes per row, the loop covers 64  -> exact fit
      ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors
  K= 128 BLOCK_SIZE_K= 32: qweight holds 64 bytes per row, the loop covers 64  -> exact fit
      ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors
  K=  96 BLOCK_SIZE_K= 64: qweight holds 48 bytes per row, the loop covers 64  -> 16 bytes past the end
      reported at vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py:236
      ERROR SUMMARY: 8 errors
  K=  48 BLOCK_SIZE_K= 32: qweight holds 24 bytes per row, the loop covers 32  -> 8 bytes past the end
      reported at vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py:236
      ERROR SUMMARY: 8 errors
```

The reported line is the unmasked `b = tl.load(b_ptrs)`, and each access lands past the end of `qweight`:

```
========= Invalid __global__ read of size 1 bytes
=========     at fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq+0xc40 in fused_moe.py:236
=========     by thread (127,0,0) in block (7,0,0)
=========     Access to 0x7f0eb2405e0f is out of bounds
=========     and is 16 bytes after the nearest allocation at 0x7f0eb2402e00 of size 12288 bytes
```

Under memcheck the launch then fails with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`; without the sanitizer the read silently returns whatever is mapped. (The error count is not a property of the defect — the driver kills the context after a variable number of reported accesses — so the fault site is the signal, not the number.)

**2. Wrong scales for an oversized K tile.** `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` against a dequantize-and-matmul reference, `block_shape = [128, 128]`, with the config lookup standing in for a tuned `configs/*.json`:

```
controls: BLOCK_SIZE_K divides group_k
  BLOCK_SIZE_K=  64  group_k=128  (requested tile inside one group)   max relative error 2.226e-07
  BLOCK_SIZE_K= 128  group_k=128  (requested tile inside one group)   max relative error 2.082e-07

bug: BLOCK_SIZE_K a multiple of group_k, which is what the comment asks for
  BLOCK_SIZE_K= 256  group_k=128  (requested tile spans 2 groups)   max relative error 2.284e-01
  BLOCK_SIZE_K= 512  group_k=128  (requested tile spans 4 groups)   max relative error 2.633e-01
```

## Environment

- `vllm-project/vllm` at `6664d397bf091cb9371cba481d4efb8233436fe6`, installed with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 pip install -e .`
- NVIDIA B200 (sm_100), driver 595.71.05
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12

items.title: [Bug]: Intermittent streamed-text corruption with MTP speculative decoding — words dropped at quote/byte-merge boundaries (raw /v1/completions repro; non-streaming clean)
items.body:
### Summary

With MTP speculative decoding enabled (`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'`), **streamed** output intermittently drops words at quote-adjacent token boundaries. The same requests non-streaming return correct text, and the same server with speculative decoding disabled streams correctly. In the affected session the corruption reproduced on **every** request for ~15 minutes across `/v1/chat/completions` and raw `/v1/completions`, with and without `tools`, at `temperature: 0` and default sampling — so it is not a parser bug (raw completions bypasses the chat template, reasoning parser, and tool parser).

### Environment

- vLLM 0.27.1 (wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12.3, Linux
- 1× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation (96GB), FLASHINFER attention backend
- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (compressed-tensors NVFP4) + its bundled MTP drafter (`model_mtp.safetensors`)
- Serve flags: `--max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --enable-auto-tool-choice --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'`

### Observed (captured verbatim from the affected session, 2026-08-14 ~21:50-22:00 local)

Prompt (chat, stream=true): `Write exactly this sentence back to me: The "implied" volatility is a "forward-looking" measure, and then add one more sentence about it.`

Content deltas received (note the missing words *implied*, *volatility is*, *forward*):

```
'The'  ' "'  '"'  ' a "'  '-looking"'  ', and it'  ' is'  ' derived from the'  ...
```

Rendered: `The " " a "-looking", and it is derived from the current market prices…`

Raw `/v1/completions` (stream=true, temperature 0, **no tools, no chat template**), prompt `Copy this sentence exactly: The "implied" volatility is a "forward-looking" measure.\nCopy: `:

```
'<think>' '\n' 'The user wants' ' me to copy' … 'The \"'  'plied\"'  ' is a \"'  'forward-looking\"'  ' measure.\n\n' …
```

(`im` of *implied* and the word *volatility* are missing between the quoted fragments.)

Same requests with `stream: false`: full, correct text. Same requests after restarting with speculative decoding **off**: streamed text correct, e.g. deltas `'The' ' "' 'im' 'plied' '"' ' volatility' ' is' ' a' ' "' 'forward' '-looking' '"' ' measure' '.'`.

### Intermittency (important for triage)

The corruption reproduced on ~every streamed request during one server session (first session after a host reboot). Later sessions with a **byte-identical** configuration stream correctly, including under targeted attempts to re-trigger:

- cache-cold prompts (unique prefixes, prefix cache unhit)
- 4-way concurrent streams
- streams racing a 26K-token chunked prefill
- temperature 0 / 0.7 / default; with and without `tools`

So the failure appears state-dependent (initialization-order or first-session state), not config-dependent. During the affected session, multi-token step deltas were being emitted (speculative accepts), and the dropped text always sat at byte-merge boundaries (quote character + following subword) — consistent with the streamed-delta slicing over multi-token steps losing a merged surface segment, while the non-streaming path (full re-render) is unaffected.

### What I can provide

Full SSE captures from both the corrupted and clean sessions, server logs for the affected window, and exact repro scripts. Happy to run instrumented builds — the host that showed the corruption is available and the model/config are pinned.

### Impact

Silent partial-text loss for streaming clients (agents, chat UIs) while token counts and non-streaming benchmarks look perfectly healthy — we found it only because an agent's quoted strings kept arriving with words missing. Currently running MTP disabled (losing +52-84% decode throughput) as the workaround.

items.title: [Bug]: Alignment specialization on causal_conv1d metadata pointers forces inference-time JIT compiles; raced shared-cache writes produced silent all-NaN outputs
items.body:
### Summary

`_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel` and `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` let Triton specialize on the 16-byte alignment of their metadata pointers (`cache_indices_ptr`, `query_start_loc_ptr`, `conv_state_indices_ptr`, ...).

Three facts make this a problem:

1. **The specialization buys nothing here.** These arrays are read one scalar at a time (a block index, an offset), so the aligned and unaligned binaries run at the same speed. Alignment specialization only pays off for wide vectorized loads (`x_ptr`, `w_ptr`, ... — not these args).
2. **Their alignment flips at runtime.** They are per-step slices of batch metadata, so the address offset depends on the batch layout of that step.
3. **Warmup can never cover the unaligned variant.** Warmup tensors are freshly allocated and therefore always aligned. So the first compile of the unaligned variant is guaranteed to happen *during inference* — this is (part of) the latency spike tracked in #43009, and `jit_monitor` (#45631) duly warns about it.

In a multi-node deployment this goes from a latency nuisance to a correctness bug.

### What we hit

GRPO RL training, Nemotron-3-Super-120B, 6 vLLM engines on 6 GB200 nodes, with a shared `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` on Lustre (for warm starts). Engines intermittently returned **all-NaN logits from the first prefill token** — only for long prompts, only on some engines, and unreproducible afterwards.

Disk forensics (no repro needed):

- These kernels compiled to disk exactly 3 times; the mtimes match the 3 NaN windows one-to-one. After the cache filled up: 40+ clean rounds, zero recurrence.
- Two cache hash dirs for the same kernel appeared **within the same minute**, differing only in the `tt.divisibility=16` attribute on `cache_indices_ptr` — two nodes concurrently compiling the aligned/unaligned variants into the same shared dir. Triton's cache group write (`__grp__*.json` + cubin) is not atomic across writers.
- Every failing request was ≥143K tokens (its `cache_indices` slice lands at an unaligned offset); every success ≤138K. Only some engines were poisoned — the race losers.

A race loser ends up running the aligned-assumption binary on unaligned `cache_indices` → reads wrong block indices → garbage → all-NaN logits, silently.

Sharing `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` across nodes is on us, and we now scope it per node. But the variant axis itself has no upside, and single-node users still pay the inference-time compile spike for it.

### Proposed fix

Add the metadata pointers to `do_not_specialize_on_alignment` — the same mechanism #50000 already applied to `num_cache_lines` in these exact kernels:

```python
@triton.jit(do_not_specialize_on_alignment=[
    "num_cache_lines",
    "cache_indices_ptr", "has_initial_states_ptr", "query_start_loc_ptr",
    "batch_ptr", "token_chunk_offset_ptr", "block_idx_first_scheduled_token",
    "block_idx_last_scheduled_token", "initial_state_idx", "num_computed_tokens",
])
def _causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel(...)

@triton.jit(do_not_specialize_on_alignment=[
    "num_cache_lines", "batch",
    "conv_state_indices_ptr", "num_accepted_tokens_ptr", "query_start_loc_ptr",
    "block_idx_last_scheduled_token", "initial_state_idx",
])
def _causal_conv1d_update_kernel(...)
```

Effect: one binary per config, compiled without the alignment assumption, correct for any address. Warmup covers it naturally, nothing left to JIT during inference, no variants to race. Zero perf cost (scalar loads only); the wide data pointers keep their specialization.

Relation to #48363: complementary. That PR warms the fwd kernel by sweeping 8 alignment combinations; with the specialization removed the sweep collapses to a single call, and `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` (not covered there) is fixed as well.

We're happy to open a PR (change verified against Triton 3.6: the flag drops the divisibility bit from the specialization key for pointer args, `triton/runtime/jit.py`).

### Environment

Observed on vLLM 0.25.1 (aarch64, GB200, Triton 3.6.0); the kernel decorators are unchanged on current `main` (f97e502969).
